Lab · Open evaluation

One demo. Hard questions. Visible results.

Public, reproducible evaluation of the document assistant: retrieval, sources and review of local-model answers.

What we measure

Twelve questions per language, including paraphrases and queries outside the library. This small set describes this prototype’s behaviour; it is not a certification or a general benchmark.

  1. Retrieval: whether the expected section is first or among the top three.
  2. Abstention: whether an unsupported question remains unanswered, including questions with vocabulary overlapping the library.
  3. Provenance: whether the displayed excerpts exist verbatim in the sources.
  4. Content: qualitative review of whether an answer resolves the question and respects the evidence. A valid citation is not enough.

Reference run

Actual outputs from a local-model run, with an explicit review for each question. Read the method, failures and limits before interpreting the numbers.

2026-11-07T16:51:41.416Z · Qwen3.5-0.8B-q4f16_1-MLC · Desktop browser on Windows with WebGPU. This run does not represent every device.

AI-assisted review (Codex), checked against each source. This is not an independent human evaluation. Four cases without sources abstain before invoking the model. The preceding run is also preserved to show output variation.

Questions and evidence

01What should I validate before using an AI response?Correct

Reference criterion

The expected structure and its values before using them. Convincing wording does not guarantee correctness.

Retrieved sources

  • Validate before acting (opens a new tab)
    If the application expects a particular structure, it must validate that structure and its values before using them. Convincing wording does not guarantee that a response is correct or suitable for taking action.

Model answer

You should validate that the structure and values match the application's expectations.

Content review

Identifies the structure and its values as the elements to validate.

02Where should integration keys be stored?Correct

Reference criterion

On the server and in its protected configuration; the browser should not receive the credential.

Retrieved sources

  • Provide context deliberately (opens a new tab)
    Integration secrets belong on the server and in its protected configuration. The browser does not need a credential to display the result of an operation.

Model answer

The text states that integration secrets should be stored on the server and in its protected configuration.

Content review

Places secrets on the server and in its protected configuration.

03What happens if the documents do not contain the answer?Partial

Reference criterion

Acknowledge missing evidence, do not invent, and allow rephrasing or checking the sources.

Retrieved sources

  • When information is missing (opens a new tab)
    If the library provides insufficient evidence, the assistant should acknowledge it. It must not invent sources, professional facts, prices or project outcomes. You can rephrase the question or open the documents to check what they contain.

Model answer

If the documents do not contain the answer, the assistant should acknowledge it.

Content review

Acknowledges missing information but omits the instruction not to invent and the alternatives of rephrasing or opening documents.

04What should I check before adding retries to an operation?Correct

Reference criterion

Whether repeating the operation could create a duplicate or perform an action twice.

Retrieved sources

  • Design the error path too (opens a new tab)
    A service can become temporarily unavailable and a request can be repeated. Before adding retries, understand whether repeating the operation might create a duplicate or perform an action twice.

Model answer

Before adding retries, you should check whether repeating the operation might create a duplicate or perform an action twice.

Content review

Answers with the risk of duplicates and performing an action twice.

05Which fields and types should an integration contract describe?Partial

Reference criterion

Fields, types, identifiers, optional values, responses, dates and error communication.

Retrieved sources

  • Make the exchange explicit (opens a new tab)
    The contract describes fields, types, identifiers, optional values and expected responses. It should also clarify how dates are represented and how errors are communicated.

Model answer

The integration contract should describe fields, types, identifiers, optional values, and expected responses.

Content review

Lists the core elements but omits date representation and error communication.

06Why should the main content exist in the HTML?Partial

Reference criterion

So headings, paragraphs and links are useful without waiting for JavaScript.

Retrieved sources

  • A foundation people can read (opens a new tab)
    The main content should exist in the document delivered to the browser. A heading, paragraph and link are useful on their own: they do not need to wait for a function to finish running.

Model answer

The main content should exist in the document delivered to the browser because it is the primary source of information that users need to access and understand.

Content review

Gives a general explanation about content but loses the specific reason: availability without waiting for JavaScript.

07When should a decorative animation stop?No answer

Reference criterion

For reduced motion, a hidden tab or an offscreen effect.

Retrieved sources

  • Motion is a layer (opens a new tab)
    Animation can explain a relationship or give an identity character. It should also be possible to stop it. A reduced-motion preference, a hidden tab or an offscreen effect are situations worth handling explicitly.

Model answer

When a decorative animation stops, it should be stopped.

Content review

The sentence is circular and identifies none of the three contexts in the source.

08Does this demo store a question and answer history?Technical error

Reference criterion

Conversations are not stored; queries are independent and navigating away or reloading clears the screen.

Retrieved sources

  • Privacy and availability (opens a new tab)
    Questions and answers are processed on the device and are not sent to an AI service. There are no keys or API usage charges. The optional download of approximately 450 MB retrieves public files from Hugging Face and may keep them in the browser cache; you can delete them from the demo. Conversations are not stored.
  • A bounded library (opens a new tab)
    Each query is independent. The application keeps no question or answer history. Navigating away or reloading clears the conversation from the screen.
  • When information is missing (opens a new tab)
    The demo does not execute actions, change data or send messages to other people. Answers are guidance and require human review before being applied to a real system.

Model answer

Model output did not pass the controls; the demo retains the excerpts.

Content review

The output was rejected with invalid_sources. The application retains excerpts confirming that conversations are not stored.

  • Provide context deliberately (opens a new tab)
    Integration secrets belong on the server and in its protected configuration. The browser does not need a credential to display the result of an operation.
  • A foundation people can read (opens a new tab)
    The main content should exist in the document delivered to the browser. A heading, paragraph and link are useful on their own: they do not need to wait for a function to finish running.

      Reproduce the evaluation

      Lightweight consultation needs no download. The AI option prepares the same demo model and processes all 24 questions in both languages here, one by one. It does not send questions to an API or store a history.

      The download is voluntary and may use mobile data. The model needs a compatible browser and available memory.

      Choose a mode to begin.

        Scope and reproduction

        The same public corpus, model and parameters as the demo. Outputs may vary between runs and devices. Download and generation times are not used as performance scores. Provenance is counted per query, including abstentions without excerpts; it does not measure answer correctness.
